From dbeb256e8dd87233d891b170c0b32a6466467036 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Long Li <longli@microsoft.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 12:40:57 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/mana_ib: Disable RX steering on RSS QP destroy

When an RSS QP is destroyed (e.g. DPDK exit), mana_ib_destroy_qp_rss()
destroys the RX WQ objects but does not disable vPort RX steering in
firmware. This leaves stale steering configuration that still points to
the destroyed RX objects.

If traffic continues to arrive (e.g. peer VM is still transmitting) and
the VF interface is subsequently brought up (mana_open), the firmware
may deliver completions using stale CQ IDs from the old RX objects.
These CQ IDs can be reused by the ethernet driver for new TX CQs,
causing RX completions to land on TX CQs:

  WARNING: mana_poll_tx_cq+0x1b8/0x220 [mana]  (is_sq == false)
  WARNING: mana_gd_process_eq_events+0x209/0x290 (cq_table lookup fails)

Fix this by disabling vPort RX steering before destroying RX WQ objects.
Note that mana_fence_rqs() cannot be used here because the fence
completion is delivered on the CQ, which is polled by user-mode (e.g.
DPDK) and not visible to the kernel driver.

Refactor the disable logic into a shared mana_disable_vport_rx() in
mana_en, exported for use by mana_ib, replacing the duplicate code.
The ethernet driver's mana_dealloc_queues() is also updated to call
this common function.

Fixes: 0266a177631d ("RDMA/mana_ib: Add a driver for Microsoft Azure Network Adapter")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Long Li <longli@microsoft.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260325194100.1929056-1-longli@microsoft.com
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>

diff --git a/include/net/mana/mana.h b/include/net/mana/mana.h
index a078af283bdd..743bfa8ad8e3 100644
--- a/include/net/mana/mana.h
+++ b/include/net/mana/mana.h
@@ -568,6 +568,7 @@ struct mana_port_context {
 netdev_tx_t mana_start_xmit(struct sk_buff *skb, struct net_device *ndev);
 int mana_config_rss(struct mana_port_context *ac, enum TRI_STATE rx,
 		    bool update_hash, bool update_tab);
+int mana_disable_vport_rx(struct mana_port_context *apc);
 
 int mana_alloc_queues(struct net_device *ndev);
 int mana_attach(struct net_device *ndev);
-- 
2.34.1



diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/qp.c b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/qp.c
index f3bb1edc7f79..e6fc3cc10795 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/qp.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/qp.c
@@ -799,6 +799,21 @@ static int mana_ib_destroy_qp_rss(struct mana_ib_qp *qp,
 	ndev = mana_ib_get_netdev(qp->ibqp.device, qp->port);
 	mpc = netdev_priv(ndev);
 
+	/* Disable vPort RX steering before destroying RX WQ objects.
+	 * Otherwise firmware still routes traffic to the destroyed queues,
+	 * which can cause bogus completions on reused CQ IDs when the
+	 * ethernet driver later creates new queues on mana_open().
+	 *
+	 * Unlike the ethernet teardown path, mana_fence_rqs() cannot be
+	 * used here because the fence completion CQE is delivered on the
+	 * CQ which is polled by userspace (e.g. DPDK), so there is no way
+	 * for the kernel to wait for fence completion.
+	 *
+	 * This is best effort — if it fails there is not much we can do,
+	 * and mana_cfg_vport_steering() already logs the error.
+	 */
+	mana_disable_vport_rx(mpc);
+
 	for (i = 0; i < (1 << ind_tbl->log_ind_tbl_size); i++) {
 		ibwq = ind_tbl->ind_tbl[i];
 		wq = container_of(ibwq, struct mana_ib_wq, ibwq);

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/microsoft/mana/mana_en.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/microsoft/mana/mana_en.c
index dca62fb9a3a9..af2a35c09773 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/microsoft/mana/mana_en.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/microsoft/mana/mana_en.c
@@ -2882,6 +2882,13 @@ static void mana_rss_table_init(struct mana_port_context *apc)
 			ethtool_rxfh_indir_default(i, apc->num_queues);
 }
 
+int mana_disable_vport_rx(struct mana_port_context *apc)
+{
+	return mana_cfg_vport_steering(apc, TRI_STATE_FALSE, false, false,
+				       false);
+}
+EXPORT_SYMBOL_NS(mana_disable_vport_rx, "NET_MANA");
+
 int mana_config_rss(struct mana_port_context *apc, enum TRI_STATE rx,
 		    bool update_hash, bool update_tab)
 {
@@ -3266,10 +3273,12 @@ static int mana_dealloc_queues(struct net_device *ndev)
 	 */
 
 	apc->rss_state = TRI_STATE_FALSE;
-	err = mana_config_rss(apc, TRI_STATE_FALSE, false, false);
+	err = mana_disable_vport_rx(apc);
 	if (err && mana_en_need_log(apc, err))
 		netdev_err(ndev, "Failed to disable vPort: %d\n", err);
 
+	mana_fence_rqs(apc);
+
 	/* Even in err case, still need to cleanup the vPort */
 	mana_destroy_vport(apc);

## Summary of Patch Modifications

### Modifications in Each File

1. **`include/net/mana/mana.h`**  
   - Added declaration of a new function `mana_disable_vport_rx()`.

2. **`drivers/net/ethernet/microsoft/mana/mana_en.c`**  
   - Implemented `mana_disable_vport_rx()` which calls `mana_cfg_vport_steering()` with parameters to disable RX steering (`TRI_STATE_FALSE`, `false`, `false`, `false`).  
   - Exported the new function via `EXPORT_SYMBOL_NS` for use by other modules (e.g., the RDMA driver).  
   - Updated `mana_dealloc_queues()` to call the new `mana_disable_vport_rx()` instead of `mana_config_rss()` for disabling vPort RX.  
   - Added a call to `mana_fence_rqs()` after disabling RX steering to ensure pending completions are flushed before destroying the vPort.

3. **`drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/qp.c`**  
   - In `mana_ib_destroy_qp_rss()`, added a call to `mana_disable_vport_rx()` **before** destroying RX work queue objects. This prevents the firmware from continuing to steer traffic to queues that are about to be freed.  
   - Added a detailed comment explaining why `mana_fence_rqs()` cannot be used here (fence completion is delivered on a userspace-polled CQ, making it impossible for the kernel to wait).

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The core fix is the introduction of `mana_disable_vport_rx()` as a shared helper. It centralizes the logic for disabling vPort RX steering, replacing ad-hoc or indirect calls (e.g., `mana_config_rss` with disable parameters) in both the ethernet and RDMA drivers.  
- The ethernet driver (`mana_dealloc_queues`) now uses the same helper and additionally inserts a `mana_fence_rqs()` call after disabling – this was previously missing and adds robustness.  
- The RDMA driver (`mana_ib_destroy_qp_rss`) uses the helper at the critical point before tearing down RX WQ objects, avoiding stale completions that could corrupt newly created TX CQs when the VF interface is later brought up.  
- The declaration in `mana.h` enables cross-module use without exposing internal implementation details, maintaining clean API boundaries between the ethernet and RDMA components.

These changes ensure that RX steering is always disabled before queue destruction in both driver paths, eliminating the race condition described in the bug report.

This patch fixes a bug in the RDMA/mana_ib driver where destroying an RSS QP left stale RX steering configuration in firmware, causing traffic to be delivered to reused CQ IDs when the ethernet driver later creates new queues. The modifications are as follows:

## Modifications per file

### `drivers/net/ethernet/microsoft/mana/mana_en.c`
- **New function `mana_disable_vport_rx()`**: Calls `mana_cfg_vport_steering()` with `TRI_STATE_FALSE` to disable vPort RX steering. Exported via `EXPORT_SYMBOL_NS` for use by the RDMA driver.  
- **Updated `mana_dealloc_queues()`**: Replaces the previous `mana_config_rss(apc, TRI_STATE_FALSE, false, false)` call with the new `mana_disable_vport_rx()` to consistently disable RX steering. Also adds a `mana_fence_rqs()` call after disabling to ensure pending completions are handled before destroying the vPort.

### `include/net/mana/mana.h`
- **Added declaration** for `mana_disable_vport_rx()` so that the function is available to the RDMA driver via `#include`.

### `drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/qp.c`
- **In `mana_ib_destroy_qp_rss()`**: Inserts a call to `mana_disable_vport_rx()` **before** destroying RX WQ objects. The accompanying comment explains that this prevents the firmware from delivering completions to stale/destroyed queues, which could otherwise land on incorrectly reused CQ IDs when the ethernet driver recreates queues. The fence mechanism (`mana_fence_rqs()`) is intentionally not used here because the CQ is polled by userspace (e.g., DPDK) and the kernel cannot wait for its completion.

## Relationships between the changes
- **Refactoring**: The logic to disable vPort RX steering is extracted into a single, shared function (`mana_disable_vport_rx()`), eliminating code duplication.  
- **Bug fix**: Both drivers now call this common function during their respective teardown paths—the ethernet driver when deallocating queues (via `mana_dealloc_queues()`) and the RDMA driver when destroying an RSS QP (via `mana_ib_destroy_qp_rss()`). This ensures that RX steering is always disabled before RX objects are destroyed, preventing stale firmware state.  
- **Subtle difference**: The ethernet driver additionally performs `mana_fence_rqs()` after disabling, which is safe because kernel driver polls the CQ; the RDMA driver cannot do this due to the user‑space CQ polling constraint. The patch’s primary fix for the RDMA path is the `mana_disable_vport_rx()` call itself.

The patch fixes a bug where destroying an RSS QP in the RDMA/mana_ib driver left stale RX steering configuration in the firmware, causing completions on reused CQ IDs. The modifications across three files introduce a shared helper to disable vPort RX steering and ensure proper cleanup ordering.

### Changes by file:

1. **drivers/infiniband/hw/mana/qp.c**  
   - In `mana_ib_destroy_qp_rss()`, added a call to `mana_disable_vport_rx()` **before** destroying the RX WQ objects.  
   - This ensures the firmware stops routing traffic to the soon-to-be-destroyed queues, preventing bogus completions on reused CQ IDs when the ethernet driver later creates new queues.

2. **drivers/net/ethernet/microsoft/mana/mana_en.c**  
   - **Added** a new exported function `mana_disable_vport_rx()` that wraps `mana_cfg_vport_steering()` to disable RX (calls with `TRI_STATE_FALSE` and all `false` flags).  
   - **Updated** `mana_dealloc_queues()` to use this new function instead of `mana_config_rss()` and moved the `mana_fence_rqs()` call after the vPort RX disable. This refactoring eliminates duplicate code and aligns the ethernet teardown with the RDMA path.

3. **include/net/mana/mana.h**  
   - Added the declaration of `mana_disable_vport_rx()` to make it accessible to both the ethernet and RDMA drivers.

### Relationships between changes:
- The core fix in `qp.c` relies on the new shared function defined in `mana_en.c` and declared in `mana.h`.  
- The ethernet driver’s teardown path is refactored to use the same helper, ensuring consistency between the two drivers.  
- The reordering in `mana_dealloc_queues()` (disable steering before fence) mirrors the RDMA logic (disable before destroying WQ objects) and prevents the same stale steering issue from occurring in the ethernet driver’s queue deallocation.

RDMA/mana_ib: Disable RX steering on RSS QP destroy

When an RSS QP is destroyed (e.g. DPDK exit), mana_ib_destroy_qp_rss()
destroys the RX WQ objects but does not disable vPort RX steering in
firmware. This leaves stale steering configuration that still points to
the destroyed RX objects.

If traffic continues to arrive (e.g. peer VM is still transmitting) and
the VF interface is subsequently brought up (mana_open), the firmware
may deliver completions using stale CQ IDs from the old RX objects.
These CQ IDs can be reused by the ethernet driver for new TX CQs,
causing RX completions to land on TX CQs:

  WARNING: mana_poll_tx_cq+0x1b8/0x220 [mana]  (is_sq == false)
  WARNING: mana_gd_process_eq_events+0x209/0x290 (cq_table lookup fails)

Fix this by disabling vPort RX steering before destroying RX WQ objects.
Note that mana_fence_rqs() cannot be used here because the fence
completion is delivered on the CQ, which is polled by user-mode (e.g.
DPDK) and not visible to the kernel driver.

Refactor the disable logic into a shared mana_disable_vport_rx() in
mana_en, exported for use by mana_ib, replacing the duplicate code.
The ethernet driver's mana_dealloc_queues() is also updated to call
this common function.

Here is the root cause:
In mana_ib_destroy_qp_rss(), the RX WQ objects are destroyed without first disabling vPort RX steering in firmware. This leaves stale steering entries that continue to route incoming traffic to the destroyed queues. When the VF interface is later brought up, the firmware may deliver completions using CQ IDs that have been reused by the ethernet driver for new TX CQs, causing RX completions to land on TX CQs and triggering warnings.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int mana_ib_destroy_qp_rss(struct mana_ib_qp *qp,
 				  struct ib_rwq_ind_table *ind_tbl,
 				  struct ib_udata *udata)
 {
 	struct mana_ib_dev *mdev =
 		container_of(qp->ibqp.device, struct mana_ib_dev, ib_dev);
 	struct mana_port_context *mpc;
 	struct net_device *ndev;
 	struct mana_ib_wq *wq;
 	struct ib_wq *ibwq;
 	int i;
 
 	ndev = mana_ib_get_netdev(qp->ibqp.device, qp->port);
 	mpc = netdev_priv(ndev);
 
+	/* Disable vPort RX steering before destroying RX WQ objects.
+	 * Otherwise firmware still routes traffic to the destroyed queues,
+	 * which can cause bogus completions on reused CQ IDs when the
+	 * ethernet driver later creates new queues on mana_open().
+	 *
+	 * Unlike the ethernet teardown path, mana_fence_rqs() cannot be
+	 * used here because the fence completion CQE is delivered on the
+	 * CQ which is polled by userspace (e.g. DPDK), so there is no way
+	 * for the kernel to wait for fence completion.
+	 *
+	 * This is best effort — if it fails there is not much we can do,
+	 * and mana_cfg_vport_steering() already logs the error.
+	 */
+	mana_disable_vport_rx(mpc);
+
 	for (i = 0; i < (1 << ind_tbl->log_ind_tbl_size); i++) {
 		ibwq = ind_tbl->ind_tbl[i];
 		wq = container_of(ibwq, struct mana_ib_wq, ibwq);
 		ibdev_dbg(&mdev->ib_dev, "destroying wq->rx_object %llu\n",
 			  wq->rx_object);
 		mana_destroy_wq_obj(mpc, GDMA_RQ, wq->rx_object);
 	}
 
 	return 0;
 }
